children: Bank Indonesia's latest rate hike highlights continued external pressure on the rupiah and marks a shift from its previous reluctance to use monetary policy to support the currency, ANZ economists Dhiraj Nim and Sanjay Mathur say in a note. Despite lower oil prices, the global environment remains challenging, given changing expectations for U.S. monetary policy, a stronger dollar and developments in the AI sector, they say. Domestic risks, including the potential MSCI downgrade of Indonesian equities and a widening current-account deficit, have added to currency volatility, with the rupiah recently approaching record lows. ANZ expects the policy rate to rise further to 6.25% in this cycle. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
